source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Install two sockets processor on MB.
Check CPU information from BIOS, OS and BMC web hardware inventory.
In BIOS:
Enter "Setup -> Processor Configuration". Check CPU information.
In Linux:
    - Check CPU information with commands:
       1. cat /proc/cpuinfo
       2. Download and install the latest dmidecode tool from (http://download.savannah.gnu.org/releases/dmidecode/).
           dmidecode -t processor
       3. lscpu
In BMC web hardware inventory:
Check the CPU healthy is "OK", and the detail CPU information is correct (include Name, Vendor, Model, Firmware verison and Status (State). 

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System can power on normally with full CPU.
2. CPU information should match with SPEC.
3. Core/Thread should be correct as the setting in BIOS setup menu.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lscpu 2>&1 | grep -iE 'socket|core|model name'; echo ---; ls /sys/devices/system/cpu 2>&1 | head; echo ---numa---; numactl -H 2>&1 | head 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL lscpu socket count + NUMA topology so the user confirms two CPU sockets are populated and enumerated; the physical install of the second socket CPU is done by the operator.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: reading socket/NUMA is read-only; the physical dual-socket install is operator.

original_test_intent: Install a supported dual-socket CPU population, prove the system powers on, and reconcile per-socket identity, health, firmware/status and core/thread topology across BIOS Setup, Linux and the BMC WebUI against the approved specification.
original_method: A qualified operator installs the two CPUs and powers on the system; the operator inspects BIOS Setup and BMC WebUI inventory while the agent can collect Linux topology/identity data and organize a per-socket cross-layer comparison.
manual_activity: Physical CPU installation/power-on and direct BIOS Setup plus BMC WebUI inspection are explicit acceptance steps. Automated Linux collection is substantial support but does not make the entire core automatable.
required_inputs: Motherboard/BIOS/BMC compatibility and two-CPU model/stepping/socket population plan
DIMM, heatsink, thermal interface, torque/service and power requirements
Expected per-socket name/vendor/model/firmware/health, cores/threads and NUMA map
Validated OS packages/tools and approved BIOS/BMC access
Qualified operator, maintenance/recovery plan and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Agent must not open the chassis, install CPUs, apply thermal material or power-cycle the SUT.
Verify socket/CPU/BIOS compatibility, ESD, orientation, pins, heatsink torque and thermal/power readiness.
Do not download an unverified 'latest' dmidecode over HTTP; use a validated package/source.
Preserve logs and stop on socket damage, boot, thermal, power, topology or management anomaly.
No automatic reseat, retry, BIOS change or power cycle.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare per-socket expected matrix and collect approved Linux `lscpu`, `/proc/cpuinfo`, `dmidecode` and NUMA evidence.
Receive operator screenshots/observations from BIOS Setup and BMC WebUI.
Reconcile identities, health and core/thread totals across all layers.
Report discrepancies without claiming installation/WebUI observation or issuing the verdict.
engineer_actions: Navigate BIOS Setup and BMC WebUI and supply the required visual evidence.
Resolve cross-layer/spec discrepancies and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Insufficient and insecure: sshpass/disabled host verification are unsuitable, `head` truncates CPU/NUMA coverage, and the command omits dmidecode, BIOS and BMC WebUI inventory/health. It cannot prove physical installation or normal power-on.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use authenticated access and retain complete unfiltered Linux topology/identity output after operator confirmation; obtain separate BIOS/BMC WebUI artifacts rather than substituting Linux data.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 20 and Machine Time 25 remain unchanged; two physical sockets and all specified layers remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a per-socket matrix keyed by socket and CPU identity, populate it from operator-captured BIOS/BMC views and complete Linux topology/DMI/NUMA output, then compare to the approved population specification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The named motherboard, firmware and supported dual-socket population.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project CPU/board population, BIOS and BMC inventory documentation; validated OS packages only.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity-locked cross-layer reconciliation and safe package provenance without removing GUI inspection.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Linux enumeration alone does not validate BIOS setup presentation, BMC WebUI health fields or physical installation quality.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Population spec, expected topology/fields, access paths, tools and operator artifacts.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware/SMBIOS naming differences require field mapping, not silent normalization.

project_override_considerations: A project may define exact CPU/DIMM/topology expectations, but must retain all three BIOS/OS/BMC layers unless an approved coverage override names what is excluded. Automated APIs cannot be assumed equivalent to required WebUI presentation.
expected_evidence: Approved CPU/board/DIMM/firmware population plan and operator installation record
BIOS Processor Configuration and BMC WebUI inventory screenshots per socket
Complete timestamped Linux lscpu/proc/dmidecode/NUMA output and version/status
Per-socket comparison and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria align on dual-socket installation, boot and cross-layer CPU/topology validation; missing model-specific values are project inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operations are clear. Compatibility/spec/tool inputs gate readiness but do not make the case semantically blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject its PARTIAL conclusion because it covers only Linux and ignores manual GUI/hardware core steps.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keep its safety and cross-layer improvements but reclassify from PARTIAL to MANUAL ONLY under the explicit V3.1 manual-observation rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automated OS evidence from required human BIOS/BMC WebUI acceptance.

review_improvement: This review prevents Linux topology from substituting for BIOS/BMC GUI and physical installation, fixes truncated/insecure command guidance and makes per-socket evidence traceable.
independent_technical_reasoning: The case is not merely human setup followed by automated core execution: physical installation/power-on and two GUI observations are themselves acceptance steps. Therefore MANUAL ONLY is the precise V3.1 capability, with strong agent-assisted collection afterward.
